claims.text: The target nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and initially have a homogeneous, single-phase solid-solution structure.
High activation barriers for atomic diffusion are inherent to the high-entropy matrix.
High diffusion barriers produce sluggish atomic rearrangement during high-temperature operation.
Nanoscale passivating surface layers, such as thin oxides, form in situ under suitable operating atmospheres.
Passivating surface layers inhibit further oxidation of the nanoparticles.
The combination of sluggish diffusion and surface passivation inhibits elemental segregation.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the single-phase solid solution.
At elevated temperatures, solid-solution stability is governed by the balance among mixing enthalpy, thermodynamic mixing contributions, and diffusion kinetics.
Kinetic effects can dominate thermodynamic contributions under electrocatalytic operating conditions.
When kinetic barriers and passivation are both effective, nanoparticles retain a uniform elemental distribution and single-phase structure.
When either kinetic hindrance or passivation is insufficient, atoms rearrange and the nanoparticles undergo phase segregation and structural change.
Effective kinetic stabilization and passivation preserve catalytic performance across 473–1923 K.
Effective kinetic stabilization and passivation preserve thermoelectric performance across 473–1923 K.
Phase separation and compositional inhomogeneity cause a corresponding decrease in performance.
The proposed stabilization mechanism is expected to apply to near-equiatomic nanoparticles but may not apply to off-stoichiometric or initially segregated systems.
Strongly oxidizing conditions can overwhelm surface passivation and therefore fall outside the mechanism's valid regime.
Changing gas atmosphere and defect density provides a controlled way to diminish passivation or kinetic hindrance.
Retention of a uniform single phase after kinetic hindrance or passivation is intentionally diminished would falsify their proposed necessity.
Significant phase segregation despite independently verified high kinetic barriers and passivation would falsify their proposed sufficiency.
